governing_table.code: Dallas Plumbing Code (Dallas City Code Chapter 54): 2021 International Plumbing Code with Dallas amendments, Ordinance No. 32422. The Dallas Building Code (Chapter 53, Ordinance No. 32421) repeats the same table as Table 2902.1 and the same rule in Section 2902.1.
governing_table.table: IPC Table 403.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures (identical rows in IBC Table 2902.1). In Dallas the table is mandatory only for Group E (educational) and Group R (residential) occupancies; for Group A (restaurants), B (offices), F, H, I, M and S it is 'recommended, but not required', and the mandatory minimum is at least one water closet for each sex.
governing_table.quote: Group A, B, F, H, I, M and S occupancies. Buildings, tenant spaces or portions of buildings where persons are employed must be provided with at least one water closet for each sex as provided for in Section 403.2. ... Group E and R occupancies. Fixtures must be provided as shown in Table 403.1 It is recommended, but not required, that the minimum number of fixtures provided also comply with the number shown in Table 403.1. Uses not shown in Table 403.1 shall be considered individually by the building official. The number of occupants shall be determined by the Dallas Building Code.

building_code_parallel.quote: Groups A, B, F, I, M and S occupancies: Buildings, floors, tenant spaces or portions thereof where persons are employed must be provided with at least one water closet for each sex except as provided in Section 2902.2. ... Group E and R occupancies must be provided with fixtures as shown in Table 2902.1. It is recommended, but not required, that the minimum number of fixtures provided also comply with the number shown in Table 2902.1.

conflict_rule.quote: The provisions of this chapter are intended to work in coordination with the provisions of the Dallas Building Code. Should any conflicts arise between the two chapters, the building official shall determine which provision applies.

adoption.quote: 2021 International Code Council codes are effective as of May 12, 2023.

amendments.text: Dallas rewrote IPC 403.1 and IBC 2902.1. The ratios in Table 403.1 / 2902.1 are not changed, but the table is binding only for Group E and R occupancies. For Group A, B, F, H, I, M and S occupancies (offices and restaurants included) the binding rule is at least one water closet for each sex where persons are employed (unless a separate-facilities exception applies); meeting the table is 'recommended, but not required'. Other Dallas changes: the code official becomes the building official; occupant load and occupancy classification come from the Dallas Building Code; the Building Code adds 2902.1.1.1 (occupant load computed under Section 1004, with a school exception based on the maximum number of students allowed per classroom), adds a condition to the 15-or-fewer separate-facilities exception (2902.2 exception 2), requires hand washing facilities in or next to water closet rooms of food establishments, a drinking fountain on each floor (not in drinking or dining establishments), and diaper changing accommodations under Section 19-38 of the Dallas City Code. Sections 403.1.1 (50/50 split, rounding up) and 424.2 (urinal substitution) are unchanged from the model code. IPC 403.2 is not amended in the plumbing ordinance, so its 15-or-fewer exception lacks the condition the Building Code adds.
amendments.quote: "403.1 Minimum number of fixtures. Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of occupancy and in the minimum number as follows: 1. Assembly occupancies. At least one drinking fountain must be provided at each floor level in an approved location. Exception: A drinking fountain need not be provided in a drinking or dining establishment. 2. Group A, B, F, H, I, M and S occupancies. Buildings, tenant spaces or portions of buildings where persons are employed must be provided with at least one water closet for each sex as provided for in Section 403.2. 3. Group E and R occupancies. Fixtures must be provided as shown in Table 403.1 It is recommended, but not required, that the minimum number of fixtures provided also comply with the number shown in Table 403.1."

sex_split.text: Total occupant load is divided in half, unless approved statistical data show another split; all-gender multi-user rooms are counted on the total occupant load.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Exceptions: 1. The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicate a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex. 2. Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number; one fixture for any fraction of the stated number of persons. For mixed occupancies, sum the fractions of each occupancy first, then round up.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded to the next whole number.

table_footnote_a.quote: The fixtures shown are based on one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction of the number of persons indicated.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace at most 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies and 50 percent in all others. Not amended by Dallas.
urinal_substitution.quote: 424.2 Substitution for Water Closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.
urinal_substitution.source_note: Read on UpCodes (secondary); Section 424.2 does not appear in the Dallas amendment ordinance.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's facilities are not required for: a total occupant load of 15 or fewer (Building Code adds: where deemed equivalent to a single-tenant building and approved by the building official); mercantile at 100 or fewer; business at 25 or fewer; single-user toilet rooms; or all-gender rooms with water closet privacy compartments.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: ... 2. Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer where the structure or tenant space is deemed to be equivalent to a building occupied by a single tenant and approved by the building official. 3. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. 4. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.

plumbing_code_version.quote: Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer.
plumbing_code_version.note: IPC 403.2 is not amended in Ordinance 32422, so it lacks the Building Code's added condition; where the two chapters conflict the building official decides.

occupant_load.text: Occupant load comes from the Dallas Building Code, Section 1004 and Table 1004.5 (floor area per occupant): business areas 150 gross sq ft; assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net; commercial kitchens 200 gross; educational classroom area 20 net; shops and vocational rooms 50 net. Schools may instead use the maximum number of students allowed per classroom where state law or city ordinance limits it. The building official may approve the actual designed number of occupants where lower.
occupant_load.quote: 2902.1.1.1 Occupant load for minimum plumbing facilities. In determining minimum plumbing facilities, the number of occupants for whom minimum plumbing facilities are provided must be computed in accordance with Section 1004. Exception: Where state law or city ordinance limits the number of students per classroom, fixtures in primary and secondary schools may be provided on the basis of the maximum number of students allowed.

table_1004_5.quote: TABLE 1004.5 MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA ALLOWANCES PER OCCUPANT ... Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) | 15 net ... Business areas | 150 gross ... Educational: Classroom area | 20 net; Shops and other vocational room areas | 50 net ... Kitchens, commercial | 200 gross
table_1004_5.section_quote: The number of occupants shall be computed at the rate of one occupant per unit of area as prescribed in Table 1004.5.
table_1004_5.source_note: Table values read on UpCodes (secondary). The Dallas ordinance amends Section 1004.5's text (building official; an exception for the actual number of occupants) but does not reprint the table.

dallas_mandatory_minimum.note: Table count is recommended, not required, in Dallas for this occupancy group; the mandatory minimum is at least one water closet for each sex (Section 403.2 / 2902.2 exceptions apply).

worked_examples.how: 50 occupants / 2 = 25 per sex (403.1.1). Water closets, '1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50': 25/25 = 1, rounded up = 1 per sex. Lavatories, '1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80': 25/40 = 0.625, rounded up = 1 per sex. Urinals: the table sets no urinal minimum; Section 424.2 lets urinals replace at most 50 percent of the required water closets: 50% x 1 = 0.5, so at most 0 urinal(s) and at least 1 water closet(s) in the men's room.

to_confirm: Publishing decision: in Dallas the table counts for offices and restaurants are a recommendation, not a requirement. The page's table should say so (required: one toilet for each sex; recommended: the table count), or show only schools as required.
Check the Table 403.1 rows, Section 424.2 and Table 1004.5 against the ICC viewer in a browser (codes.iccsafe.org, 2021 IPC Chapter 4 and 2021 IBC Chapter 10); they were read on UpCodes.

Ask Dallas Building Inspection how plan review treats the 'recommended, but not required' sentence for Group A and B in practice, and which 15-or-fewer exception applies (IPC 403.2 as published, or Building Code 2902.2 exception 2 with building official approval).
The plumbing ordinance lists Groups 'A, B, F, H, I, M and S'; the building ordinance lists 'A, B, F, I, M and S' (no H). Irrelevant to offices, restaurants and schools.

Other bodies may set higher counts than the city code for the same building: Texas health rules for food establishments, OSHA for employee toilets, Texas Education Agency facility standards for schools. Not researched here.
